source_text: Mira tunc ibi cerneres et exquisita conpendia saeuiendi. Namque cum manum carnificis gladiumque ipsum tot ceruicibus deditum numerosus iustorum populus urgueret, artifex feritas dispositas agminum series per ordinem dirigebat, scilicet ut sacrilegi percussoris ictus uelut impetu quodam furoris pia colla percuteret. Deinde ut ne inexplicabile fieret cruentum illud et barbarum ministerium, hanc sibi expeditionem sceleris inuenit. Nam si uno in loco percussurus ipse consisteret, inmensam stragem corporum cumulus aceruaret; ipse denique spatium tanta strage conpletus alueus denegaret. Tunc oculis sub ictu ferri de more uelatis, nullae tamen aciem liberae mentis clausere tenebrae, sed largus atque inaestimabilis splendor inmensae lucis effulsit. Nam et plerique cum proximis et assistentibus sibi fratribus, quamuis carnaliter in uisum acies non pateret, uidere se tamen mira quaedam loquebantur, quod sibi apparerent equi desuper niueo colore candentes, quibus ueherentur iuuenes candidati. Nec defuere ex eodem martyrum numero qui collegarum relationem adtestarentur auribus et ex audito equorum fremitu ac sono recognoscerent. Ibi tunc et Marianus, prophetico spiritu iam repletus, fidenter ac fortiter praedicabat proximam iusti sanguinis ultionem, uariasque saeculi plagas uelut de caeli iam culmine minabatur, luem, captiuitates, famem, terraeque motus et cynomiae uenena cruciantia. Qua praedicatione non tantum gentilibus insultabat fides martyris, sed etiam fratribus incentiuum aemulandae uirtutis et quasi classicum praecanebat, ut inter tantas saeculi plagas a iustis dei tam bonae atque pretiosae mortis raperetur occasio.
pass_a_gloss: You would then have beheld strange sights there and refined shortcuts of savagery. For while a numerous people of the just pressed close around the executioner's hand and the very sword surrendered to so many necks, ingenious cruelty kept directing the drawn-up rows of the columns in sequence, so that the blow of the sacrilegious slayer might fall upon the faithful necks as if with a rush of rage. Next, lest that bloody and barbarous service become unmanageable, it devised for itself this way to expedite the crime. For if the striker himself stayed in one place to strike, the piled mass would heap up a huge wreck of bodies; in the end the trough-like place, filled by so great a slaughter, would deny him space. Then, though their eyes were veiled in the usual manner beneath the stroke of the iron, nevertheless no darkness shut the gaze of the free mind, but a generous and inestimable splendor of immense light flashed out. For many, together with the brothers beside them and standing near them, although sight was not open to the eye in a bodily way, still declared that they saw certain marvels, namely that horses shining with snow-white color appeared to them from above, upon which youths clothed in white were borne. Nor were there wanting from the same company of martyrs men who confirmed the report of their comrades by hearing and knew it again from the heard neighing and noise of horses. There then Marianus too, already filled with a prophetic spirit, confidently and bravely kept proclaiming the near avenging of just blood, and kept threatening diverse scourges of the world as if already from the height of heaven: pestilence, captivities, famine, and earthquakes and the tormenting poisons of the dog-fly. By this proclamation the martyr's faith not only mocked the pagans but also sounded in advance for the brothers a spur to rivalrous courage and as it were a trumpet-signal, so that amid so many scourges of the world an opportunity for so good and precious a death might be seized by God's just ones.
pass_b_english: Then you might have looked upon astonishing sights and the calculated economies of brutality. A great crowd of the righteous thronged the headsman's arm and the very blade consigned to so many throats, so contriving cruelty marched the ordered files of the ranks through in turn, that each sacrilegious blow might descend upon a faithful neck as if driven by a gust of frenzy. And lest that gory and barbarous labor clog beyond handling, it hit upon this dispatch for its crime: had the slayer kept his footing in one spot to strike, the mounting heap would have raised a vast wall of corpses, and the riverbed itself, choked with the carnage, would at last have refused him standing-room. Then, although their eyes were bound in the customary manner beneath the falling steel, no darkness sealed the vision of the unbound mind, and a lavish splendor beyond reckoning, a flood of light, burst forth. Many among them, side by side with the brethren next to them and assisting them, though no bodily sight lay open to their eyes, insisted that they beheld wonders: horses dazzling snow-white appeared above them, bearing youths robed in white, and others of that same martyr company, who had not seen, attested their companions' account by what they heard, recognizing the neighing and clatter of horses.

There Marianus also, already filled with a prophetic spirit, proclaimed with assurance and courage the imminent vindication of righteous blood, and denounced from what seemed already the height of heaven the manifold afflictions of the world to come: pestilence and captivities and famine and earthquakes and the tormenting venoms of the dog-fly. By that proclamation the martyr's faith both defied the pagans and sounded beforehand among the brethren a summons to emulous valor, like a trumpet-call, that amid such afflictions of the world the righteous of God might seize the occasion for a death so good and so precious.
